after: Liquid component molar delivery is C × Q. In a fully liquid-filled, unpacked reactor, V/QL is nominal liquid space time. Gas molar delivery uses the stated reference temperature and pressure; reactive-gas equivalents additionally include the active mole fraction. The inlet-reference index V/(QL + Qg,STP) is a bookkeeping index, not a physical residence time under operating pressure. Ideal-gas scaling gives Qg,ch = Qg,STP(Tch/TSTP)(PSTP/Pabs), with absolute temperature and pressure. A time formed using this local gas volume remains a nominal homogeneous-flow estimate: it assumes negligible phase slip and neglects dissolution, gas consumption and axial variations unless separately modeled. The ratio Qg,ch/(QL + Qg,ch) is a no-slip volumetric gas fraction, not measured holdup. For a packed bed or gas–liquid reactor, liquid contact time instead requires accessible liquid volume or holdup, with residence-time-distribution measurements needed to characterize dispersion. A standard-volume gas feed and a compressed volume must never be substituted into the same equivalent calculation without converting their reference states.
